clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1994
clusters.reason: Your grandfather's stroke in June 1991 opened a long stretch: within weeks you started at the conservatory leaning hard on Rafe, then a wrist injury stopped your playing and you lost your footing. Rafe moved out after a blow-up, you got high in your room, and by early 1992 you were lost and low with him gone and your mother about to remarry. Your grandmother Winifred had surgery for thyroid cancer around the same time. Through 1992 you drifted at community college, nights playing pool and days asleep. By early 1994 you were stung your dad had never heard of your film, then found your drive again with an exchange abroad and raced through your degree. Your cousin Bella was treated for melanoma in these months; your grandmother's thyroid surgery and your mother's wedding in autumn 1992 sit in the same stretch but are not shifts themselves. The period settles as you found your footing again by 1994.

clusters.reason: Around your eighteen-month relationship with Joelle ending in summer 1999: your insomnia began getting in the way before concerts, though you were playing the best you ever had and winning competitions. clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's death, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Your grandmother was found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002 while you were running out of steam for performing, less content by the month. You had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra in your home town and were done with performing. You left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, met Marisol at a winter party, moved with her to Fenwick, then split within the year and sank into a deep depression. You returned to Thornbury, could not face your family though they seemed a world away, and relied on friends—Silas, Corbin and others—while your father spoke with Corbin during your stay. You began swimming, requested help with therapy costs, and returned to your therapist Victor. Your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home and you dropped in briefly on her sickroom hung over on your way to the airport; she died of the cancer in February 2004. The period settles as you began to recover with your therapist and took up nursing school.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008–2010
clusters.reason: Your grandmother Lorna died in January 2008, and your grandfather Clifford around the same time. Within months you were at Alder Creek building with Silas and too drained for conversation with your mother; she pressed to visit you, you told her the timing was wrong, she drove out regardless and you kept the door shut on her. You left for nursing school in Marlow Sound that summer and stopped speaking to your mother; the silence held roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke in early 2009 with months of rehabilitation. Your partner's brother Leo's first child was born in 2010. The period settles as you and your mother rebuilt contact over the following year, though at a distance.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: You married Wren in March 2017 and saw your mother a bit less once she came along. In autumn 2019 Wren's family gathered at the lake house for her mother's retirement: a street party, then a fundraiser, then the drive to the lake. Wren was swamped, one thing after another, and you laid out a plan too strictly to settle her, overfunctioning in a way you'd like to change. Her father, brother and she talk all day and nothing happens to one the others don't hear. She settled once the weekend had a plan and the dinner went well, but you were awake from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose; you don't feel you belong. She grew anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions. Your sister Tara flies for a regional airline and married James the previous summer; she and James live in Rennick. Your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in her forties that year. Your aunt Imogen's memory was slipping and getting worse; she lashes out when muddled and Hal had never known her like this. Your job had steadied and paid well by June, far less strain, though you constantly feel you ought to be driving your projects forward. You started a sleeping pill. By October you were aiming for shorter, more regular calls with your mother. Your sister's baby was on the way, Russell's first grandchild. The period shows your own anxiety building around your partner's intensity and closeness with her family, while her own troubles and those in the wider family pile up around the same months.
